assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md parsed CVE data table lists: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = < 0.11.14, Fixed version = 0.11.14. All four values are correctly identified.

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Ecosystem Detection section states: 'The vulnerable library is quinn-proto, a Rust crate. Based on the library name and component context (pscomponent:org/rhtpa-server, a Rust backend service), the ecosystem is identified as Cargo.'

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: Security matrix defines 7 versions: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). The version-impact.md table includes all 7 versions with no omissions.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md explicitly states: 'Dependency versions are extracted using the pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version (Important Rule 13), not branch HEAD.' The table includes a Pinned Tag column with values v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12 matching the security matrix.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md row for 2.2.2 shows: 'v0.4.9 | -- | YES | retag of 2.2.1 (same as 2.2.1; backend tag v0.4.8 reused)'. The evidence source note confirms: 'Version 2.2.2 was skipped (Important Rule 5) because it is a retag of 2.2.1; its affected status is carried forward from 2.2.1.'

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md shows Current (PSIRT-assigned): [RHTPA 2.0.0] and Proposed (lock-file-verified): [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2], with an explicit diff block showing '- RHTPA 2.0.0 (REMOVE)' and '+ RHTPA 2.2.0/2.2.1/2.2.2 (ADD)' with evidence for each.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md Step 3.1 describes dynamic version discovery via jira.getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields API. The mutation uses placeholder IDs (<RHTPA-2.2.0-jira-id>) and states: 'Version IDs are resolved from the dynamic version registry discovered in Step 3.1 -- they are referenced by name (RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2) and mapped to their Jira IDs at runtime.'

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md upstream task includes Repository (rhtpa-backend), Target Branch (release/0.4.z), Acceptance Criteria (3 items), and Dependencies section. Downstream task includes Repository (rhtpa-release.0.4.z), Target Branch (main), Acceptance Criteria (2 items), and Dependencies listing both upstream task and TC-8001. A Blocks link connects upstream to downstream.

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md states: 'The ecosystem is Cargo (source dependency), so two tasks are created for the 2.2.x stream.' Task 1 is 'Upstream Backport (2.2.x stream)' and Task 2 is 'Downstream Propagation Subtask (2.2.x stream)'. A Blocks link is created: 'jira.create_link(inwardIssue: <upstream-task-key>, outwardIssue: <downstream-task-key>, type: "Blocks")'

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: All mutations are framed as proposals: data-extraction.md uses 'Proposed actions:'; affects-versions.md uses 'Proposed Jira Mutation' with 'After engineer confirmation'; remediation.md uses 'Proposed Jira creation (requires engineer confirmation)' for both tasks, 'Proposed comment on TC-8001 (requires engineer confirmation)' for the cross-stream comment, and frames post-triage actions as 'would be proposed'.

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md begins with 'Step 0.7 -- Early Assignment' (line 1) before 'Step 1 -- Data Extraction' (line 36). Step 0.7 describes: (1) retrieving current user account ID, (2) assigning TC-8001 to the current user via jira.edit_issue, (3) discovering the Assigned transition via jira.get_transitions, and (4) transitioning TC-8001 from New to Assigned via jira.transition_issue.
